anchorData: PHOTOS (one passport picture, three prints). Print S (stamp): 3 cm wide x 4 cm tall, face height 2.4 cm, diagonal 5 cm, area 12 cm2, price KES 30. Print P (postcard): 6 cm wide x 8 cm tall, face height 4.8 cm, diagonal 10 cm, area 48 cm2, price KES 120. Print L (large): 9 cm x 12 cm, diagonal 15 cm, area 108 cm2, price KES 270. Optional half-size print H: 1.5 cm x 2 cm, area 3 cm2, price KES 7.50. Pricing rule: paper is charged at KES 2.50 per cm2. Checks: 12 x 2.5 = 30; 48 x 2.5 = 120; 108 x 2.5 = 270; 3 x 2.5 = 7.50. S to P: LSF = 2 (6/3 = 8/4 = 10/5 = 4.8/2.4 = 2); area ratio 48/12 = 4 = 2^2; cost ratio 120/30 = 4. S to L: LSF = 3; area ratio 108/12 = 9 = 3^2; cost ratio 270/30 = 9. P to S: LSF = 1/2. S to H: LSF = 1/2. DISTORTED PHOTO (not similar): 6 cm x 4 cm, made by doubling only the width (width ratio 2, height ratio 1), area 24 cm2. TRIANGLES: 3-4-5 and 6-8-10 (similar, LSF 2). RECTANGLES: 3 x 4 and 6 x 7 (not similar; ratios 2 and 1.75). MODEL MATATU: real matatu 7 m long = 700 cm; model 1:25 gives 28 cm long (700/25 = 28). SHADOWS (Kericho): student 1.5 m tall casts a 2 m shadow; tree casts a 12 m shadow at the same time; the triangles are similar with LSF 6 (12/2); tree height = 1.5 x 6 = 9 m. VOLUME: cube of side 2 cm has volume 8 cm3; LSF 2 gives side 4 cm and volume 64 cm3 (64/8 = 8 = 2^3); LSF 3 cube side 6 cm, volume 216 cm3 (27 times). Jerrycans: small similar jerrycan 5 L, height 25 cm; LSF 2 container height 50 cm, volume 5 x 8 = 40 L. ENLARGEMENT GRID (origin O(0,0)): triangle A(1,1), B(3,1), C(2,3). Scale factor 2: A'(2,2), B'(6,2), C'(4,6). Scale factor 1/2 applied to A'B'C' returns A(1,1), B(3,1), C(2,3). Scale factor -2: A''(-2,-2), B''(-6,-2), C''(-4,-6). Finding the centre: object A(2,1), B(4,1), C(3,3); image A'(3,2), B'(7,2), C'(5,6); lines AA' (y = x - 1) and BB' meet at centre (1,0); scale factor = A'B'/AB = 4/2 = 2. MAPS: Nairobi to Mombasa road distance 440 km; map scale 1:5,000,000 gives 8.8 cm (8.8 x 5,000,000 = 44,000,000 cm = 440 km). Kisumu to Nairobi 350 km gives 7 cm on the same map. Classroom: actual 8 m x 6 m = 48 m2; scale drawing 1:50 gives 16 cm x 12 cm = 192 cm2; ASF = 50^2 = 2500; 192 x 2500 = 480,000 cm2 = 48 m2. Floor tiles at KES 800 per m2: 48 x 800 = KES 38,400.
characters: Achieng: Grade 10 student in Kisumu who needs passport photos for KCSE registration and a school ID; she is the main character. Mr Otieno: photographer at a Kisumu shop who prints the same photo as stamp size S (3 x 4 cm, KES 30) and postcard size P (6 x 8 cm, KES 120); he charges KES 2.50 per cm2 of paper. Ms Wanjiru: the maths teacher who runs the Driving Question Board. Kericho tree and student: the 9 m tree and the 1.5 m student for shadow work. Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu: map and cost contexts (440 km, 350 km). Model matatu 1:25 (28 cm). Jerrycan: 5 L small vs 40 L similar large. Lessons may use these names and facts only and must not change any number.
outcome: Achieng finds that print P is an enlargement of print S with linear scale factor 2: every length doubles (3 to 6, 4 to 8, diagonal 5 to 10) and all angles stay the same, so the shape is unchanged. Area is multiplied by 2^2 = 4 (12 cm2 to 48 cm2), so Mr Otieno's paper charge rises from KES 30 to KES 120, which is four times and not double; the same idea gives volume scale factor k^3 (a LSF 2 jerrycan holds 8 times as much, 5 L to 40 L). Doubling the width only (6 x 4 cm) gives a stretched, non-similar picture.
conventions: LSF (linear scale factor) k = image length / object length, same units and corresponding sides in the same order. ASF = k^2; VSF = k^3. Say 'object' and 'image' (image is labelled with a prime: A to A'). Similar figures: equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Enlargement needs a centre and a scale factor; k > 1 enlargement, 0 < k < 1 reduction (still called enlargement with fractional scale factor), negative k gives an inverted image on the opposite side of the centre. Use cm, cm2, cm3, m, km, litres (1 L = 1000 cm3), KES. The anchor photo is always named S (3 x 4), P (6 x 8), L (9 x 12), H (1.5 x 2). Map scale written 1:n; actual = map x n. Paper cost always KES 2.50 per cm2 and cost scales with area, not with length. Use 'similar' for same shape and 'congruent' only for same shape and size. Use ASF, not 'area factor'. Do not rename the Driving Question Board (DQB).
